headline: State Park Day Use and Camping Coordination
reservation: Valley of Fire State Park requires a daily entrance fee paid at the gate; no advance reservation is currently needed for entry, but campgrounds are first-come, first-served or via a separate portal. Always check the official Nevada State Parks website for the latest updates on trail closures or new booking requirements.

days.title: Petroglyphs and Ancient Vistas

stops.name: Atlatl Rock
stops.detail: Climb the stairs to view ancient petroglyphs and a depiction of the prehistoric atlatl throwing tool.

stops.name: The Beehives
stops.detail: Explore unique cross-bedded sandstone formations that resemble giant petrified hives.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for park navigation; conditions vary
days.note: Early starts are essential to avoid the midday desert heat, even in shoulder seasons.

days.title: Swirling Sandstone and Slot Canyons
days.start: Suggested: 7 AM from the Visitor Center

stops.name: The Fire Wave
stops.detail: Walk the trail to the striped, marble-like sandstone waves that are the park's most famous landmark.

stops.name: White Domes Loop
stops.detail: Hike through a varied landscape featuring a slot canyon and remnants of historic film sets.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for scenic road stops; conditions vary
days.note: The Fire Wave trail may close when temperatures exceed safety thresholds; check signs at the trailhead.

days.title: Red Cliffs and Rainbow Vistas

stops.name: Rainbow Vista
stops.detail: Enjoy a panoramic overlook where the desert's multi-colored hills meet the horizon.

stops.name: Elephant Rock
stops.detail: Photograph this distinct formation located near the park's east entrance after a short walk.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for transit from Las Vegas; conditions vary
days.note: Midday sun flattens the colors; these sites are best viewed when shadows provide depth to the rock.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking at the Fire Wave/Seven Wonders lot is extremely limited and often fills by 9 AM on weekends. Have a backup plan to visit the Beehives or Atlatl Rock if primary lots are full.

intel.title: Basin Dead Zones
intel.text: Cell service is non-existent in most of the park's canyons and along White Domes Road. The Visitor Center offers the only reliable point for emergency communication.

intel.title: Gateway Supply Points
intel.text: There are no gas stations inside the park. Ensure your tank is full before leaving Overton or North Las Vegas, as the desert terrain increases fuel consumption.

intel.title: Heat Safety Windows
intel.text: Summer temperatures regularly exceed 100°F (38°C). Limit hiking to the two hours following sunrise and avoid all strenuous activity during the afternoon heat.

intel.title: Slot Canyon Hazards
intel.text: Flash flooding is a risk in areas like the White Domes slot canyon even if it is not raining locally. Monitor regional weather and heed all ranger warnings.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Harry Reid International (LAS), purchase bulk water and snacks in North Las Vegas, and arrive at the West Entrance fee station.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for the paved Valley of Fire Highway; avoid driving off-road into soft sand where towing is difficult.
plan.goldenHour: White Domes Road for sunset photography; the sandstone glows brightest as the sun nears the horizon in the west.
